oliver: Heads-up — we just got a couple kv-prefix-cache alerts for high eviction rate, alert id `KV_PREFIX_EVICT_HIGH`. Anyone know where the best place is to look for eviction logs + traces? @janet @mike :thinking:

janet: Grafana has the KV Cache dashboard — panels for `prefix_hit_ratio`, `evictions_total`, and `prefetch_latency`. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-cache  For raw logs use Loki: https://loki.redwood.ai/explore — filter `app=kv-service` + `log_level=warn` and search for `evict` or `prefetch`. Example LogQL:```{app="kv-service"} |= "evict" | json | line_format "${message}"```

mike: Also check Honeycomb traces in dataset `kv-serving`. Traces show if evictions line up with long tail RPCs from prefetch workers. Quick trace link pattern: https://ui.honeycomb.io/redwood/datasets/kv-serving/trace?trace_id=<id>
  If you want a quick metric check in Prometheus:```sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[5m])) by (cluster)```

sudha: For the alert itself, we should stop triggering on single short spikes. Suggest switching alert from `avg_over_time(evictions_total[1m]) > 10` to something like `increase(evictions_total[5m]) > 50` or a rate threshold: `sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[5m])) > 0.5` depending on cluster size. Also add a suppression window of 10m so noisy autoscaler events don't spam.

observability-bot: Alert KV_PREFIX_EVICT_HIGH acknowledged by @mike at 1837001250. Current alert context: cluster=us-west-2, evictions=73 (5m). Related runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-evictions

oliver: Awesome, thanks. I'll pull the recent traces + logs and open a small PR to adjust the alert window/rate. @mike can you review the dashboard write access? Also, if anyone sees evictions tied to a specific model or tenant id, drop the trace id here. :thumbsup:
